column1: # Model tiers per harness for the vitruvian-core specialist roster.
# Only the lead thinks on Claude. Every specialist's work runs on Gemini:
# - lead:  the lead and beacon. Claude Opus in Claude Code and OpenCode; Antigravity has
#          no Opus, so there it is Antigravity's `pro` model.
# - build: specialists that write and test changes (apps, infrastructure, build, cluster).
#          Antigravity's Orchestrator (Carbon): Carbon plans, Gemini 4 Hydrogen edits and
#          tests, and hard parts go back to Carbon. Each call has a fixed planning cost
#          (~12k output tokens for a one-word answer), so short tasks belong elsewhere.
# - deep:  specialists whose work is judgement (QA, security review, acceptance). Gemini 4 Carbon.
# - light: specialists whose work is lighter (docs, release tracking). Gemini 4 Hydrogen.
# A tier with a `gemini` row does its work on that Gemini model. Antigravity runs it natively
# (its own column). In Claude Code and OpenCode the generator writes a driver instead: a small
# Haiku agent with no editing tools that hands the work to the `gemini` model through
# agy-delegate, checks the result and reports back. So for those tiers the claude-code and
# opencode columns are the driver's model, not the model doing the work.
# Format rules:
# - Antigravity agent files accept only model inherit|flash|pro (Antigravity's own aliases; it picks
#   which Gemini model each means) and have no effort field (use "-").
# - OpenCode needs full provider/model ids (e.g. anthropic/claude-opus-5-5).
# - Claude Code accepts opus|sonnet|haiku|fable|inherit or a full claude-* id,
#   plus effort medium|high|xhigh|max.
# - gemini takes an exact `agy models` id and effort "-"; never a low, lite or flash-lo model.
# - Effort "low" is forbidden.
